entries.title: PC Gaming
entries.final_prompt:
Create a premium collectible hobby illustration. The artwork should feel cinematic, aspirational, emotionally warm, commercially polished, and immediately readable on a small mobile card. Use a strong focal subject, crisp subject separation, rich but controlled colour, atmospheric depth, premium lighting, and clear visual storytelling. Sell the emotional fantasy of doing the hobby rather than merely depicting an object. Aim for the feel of a miniature lifestyle hero illustration inside one coherent collectible-art universe, not a poster, advertisement, editorial cover, card face, or designed page. Keep edges and subject readability cleaner than soft editorial painting. No text, no logo, no typography, no card border, no rarity badge, no watermark, no UI.

The hobby or interest name is semantic context only and must never appear visually. Never render the hobby name, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, body copy, text box, lower-third, or typography-like decoration. Do not reserve blank layout space for text and do not turn the composition into a poster, advertisement, magazine cover, card face, or editorial page. Any incidental real-world surface that could carry writing must be blank, abstract, cropped away, turned away, or too indistinct to read.

Treat every monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, camera display, dashboard, terminal, and digital panel as a physical prop rather than a semantic canvas. Prefer no visible screen surface at all. Recognition must come from the person, physical tool, device, prototype, controller, camera, microphone, hardware, object, or real-world action. If a screen is genuinely unavoidable, show only its back, edge, steep oblique angle, dark/blank surface, or a heavily defocused field of broad colour/image shapes; keep it small and secondary. Never present a front-facing readable display, interface, editing timeline, waveform panel, code window, terminal, menu, chat, dashboard, spreadsheet, labels, controls, icons, or text-like UI structure.

Use this overall composition approach: Show a seated PC gamer actively playing through physical desktop-gaming hardware while every display surface is physically absent. The generic desktop tower, full-size keyboard, mouse, mouse mat, headphones, hand positions, seated posture, and focused reaction must carry the entire concept. This is play, not building, repairing, coding, streaming, or office work. Side or rear-three-quarter medium framing that clearly shows the player, hands on keyboard and mouse, headphones, and generic desktop tower while cropping the entire forward display zone outside the image. The emotional feeling should be focus, challenge, enthusiasm, hands-on play. Make the hobby immediately recognizable through PC gaming is identified by the combined physical language of a desktop tower, keyboard, mouse, headphones, active seated posture, and gaming reaction, never by gameplay imagery or a visible screen..

Compose the specific scene this way: A focused player wears plain headphones and actively uses a generic full-size keyboard and mouse beside one visible unbranded desktop tower. Hands, posture, and reaction communicate active PC play. The physical monitor position is completely outside the composition, and no substitute display device appears. Low side three-quarter medium shot including face/reaction, hands, keyboard, mouse, headphones, and desktop tower, with the view cropped before any monitor area. Use Painterly cinematic room light with controlled practical accents; no monitor glow and no neon cyberpunk treatment..

Use this colour and material direction: engaging interactive atmosphere with clear player-input and game-context readability. the player's interaction with the game must be visually obvious, show social interaction when it is intrinsic to the interest, but do not force extra people into solo digital play, keep game feedback generic and non-IP unless a rights-cleared recipe explicitly says otherwise.

Depict this activity: A focused PC gamer wearing plain headphones actively plays using a generic full-size keyboard and mouse beside one visible unbranded desktop tower, with hands, seated posture, and reaction communicating active computer gaming while the entire monitor zone stays outside the frame

Place it in this believable setting: A believable home PC-gaming corner with a seated player, generic desktop tower, full-size keyboard, mouse, mouse mat, headphones, chair, and simple room details; no monitor, television, laptop, tablet, phone, projector, display panel, gameplay screen, or other screen-bearing device anywhere

The emotional tone should feel connection, challenge, fun, shared excitement.

Use this activity-specific composition: The dedicated PC-play scene must be carried by the player, desktop tower, keyboard, mouse, headphones, active hands, seated posture, and focused gaming reaction. Do not depict building, repairing, assembling, coding, streaming, or presenting an object. Crop before the monitor zone.

Use this activity-specific camera treatment: Low side three-quarter medium shot showing player, keyboard, mouse, headphones, and desktop tower together while excluding the entire display area.

Keep these hobby-recognition cues visible: active play, engaged participant reaction, clear game or play-surface cue, generic desktop computer tower, full-size keyboard and mouse actively used for play, plain headphones, focused seated gaming posture and reaction.

The scene must include: a visible PC Gaming play interaction, one generic unbranded desktop tower, active hands on keyboard and mouse, plain headphones, seated player reaction, zero screen-bearing devices anywhere in frame.

Follow these additional scene constraints: This is a dedicated screenless PC-gaming scene, not a collectible-object build and not streaming. The player is already gaming. Do not place any gadget in the player's hands other than normal keyboard/mouse interaction, and do not invent a screen.

Do not depict any of the following: generic social gathering with no game cue, readable game branding or copyrighted characters, screen soup, monitor, television, laptop, tablet, phone, projector, display panel, game screen, game HUD, code, IDE, terminal, waveform, chat window, streaming interface, screen glow, building or repairing a gadget, object assembly, steampunk device, brand logo, manufacturer badge, projector screen, streaming UI, office-work posture, RGB brand logo, recognisable manufacturer badge.

Also avoid these global failure modes: text, logos, watermarks, card borders, rarity labels, UI elements, floating unrelated objects, duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested, flat procedural vector art, bland corporate illustration, generic stock-photo composition, muddy focal hierarchy, overabstract imagery, generic concept wallpaper, confusing mixtures of different hobbies, pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image, readable real-world brand names, logos, or trademarks, recognisable copyrighted film/game/cartoon characters or franchise costumes, collage, split-screen, comic-panel, or multi-panel layouts, photoreal stock-photo rendering unless explicitly requested by the hobby recipe, the hobby or interest name rendered anywhere in the image, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, or body copy, poster, advertisement, magazine-cover, card-face, or editorial-page layout, text boxes, caption bands, lower-thirds, or deliberate blank space reserved for typography.

readable game branding or copyrighted characters
duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested
pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image
readable real-world brand names, logos, or trademarks

the hobby or interest name rendered anywhere in the image
title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, or body copy

image_diagnostics.detector_note: Diagnostic only: edge bands require low within-row luma variance/range plus stable tone across contiguous rows; darkness is not required.
